events.factual_description: Blue Note Tokyo presents Tropical Jazz Big Band's THE 忘年会LIVE 2026 on December 16 and 17, 2026, with sets at 6:00 PM and 8:30 PM on both nights. The venue describes the engagement as the band's annual year-end live tradition and announces a large ensemble led by percussionist Carlos Kanno, with piano, bass, drums, timbales, bongos, congas, trumpet, trombone and saxophone sections. Blue Note notes that the group was formed in 1995 around Kanno, formerly of Orquesta de la Luz, and continues after its 30th-anniversary year. One additional member remains TBA on the current event page.

en.why_it_matters: This belongs because the sound is built around a genuinely Japanese Latin-jazz lineage rather than a generic big-band format. Carlos Kanno came out of Orquesta de la Luz, and Tropical Jazz Big Band turns that percussion vocabulary into a large brass-and-reeds machine: congas, bongos and timbales are structural voices, not decoration. The year-end Blue Note tradition gives the engagement a specific Tokyo identity while the band's longevity makes it a useful living thread between Japan's Latin boom and its current large-ensemble scene.
en.trip_verdict: Worth keeping on the December Tokyo board, especially if the trip has room for a high-energy brass-and-percussion night. With four sets across two nights and a recurring year-end tradition, it is easy to fit around scarcer masters, premieres or one-off encounters rather than reorganizing the itinerary around it.

es.why_it_matters: Entra porque el sonido nace de una genealogía japonesa de jazz latino bastante concreta, no de una big band genérica. Carlos Kanno viene de Orquesta de la Luz y Tropical Jazz Big Band convierte ese vocabulario de percusión en una maquinaria grande de metales y maderas: congas, bongós y timbales son voces estructurales, no adorno. La tradición de fin de año en Blue Note le da una identidad muy de Tokio, y la longevidad de la banda conecta el boom latino japonés con la escena actual de grandes ensambles.
es.trip_verdict: Vale tenerla en el tablero de diciembre en Tokio, sobre todo si queda espacio para una noche de metales y percusión con mucho empuje. Como hay cuatro sets en dos noches y es una tradición recurrente de fin de año, se puede acomodar alrededor de maestros más escasos, estrenos o encuentros verdaderamente irrepetibles sin rehacer el itinerario.
